newsitem.title: UK: Standard Chartered hurt by strong pound.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered hurt by strong pound.

text.p: Standard Chartered Plc, the London-based bank with a big Asia-Pacific region franchise, on Wednesday reported first-half, pre-tax profits of 435 million pounds ($707 million), seriously affected by the strength of sterling.

The figure compared to 448 million pounds last year but that included a exceptional gain of 46 million pounds. StanChart said trading profit was up eight percent but would have risen 16 percent if exchange rates had remained constant.

StanChart said it was raising its interim dividend by 24 percent to 5.25 pence per share from 4.25 pence for the first half of last year. Both dividend and pre-tax profit figures were within market expectations.
Of Standard Chartered's trading profit, 156 million pounds, or 36 percent, comes from Hong Kong and the bank said it was optimistic about the development of the Hong Kong economy.
StanChart said its Treasury operations had a particularly good first half with the bank making good profits from recent volatility in some Asian currency markets.

Cost in the bank were higher, as the management had previously flagged, but income rose more to leave the cost to income ratio better at 53.7 percent compared to 55.7 percent. -- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8864.
